To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dilaton field is a crucial ingredient in the theory, that it allows for the localization of the massless and massive Kalb-Ramand modes into the 4D brane, and that it also allows to prevent tachyon contributions in the whole spectrum.

i) the dilaton coupling is the main responsible for the localization of the gauge fields on the brane; ii) the coupling to the dilator is different for both gauge fields; and iii) the coupling to gravity is the same for both gauge fields.
(i) The dilaton coupling to the Kalb-Ramon field is different to the dilaton coupling to Maxwell field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a Maxwell-Kalab-Ramond theory in a 5D curved space-time with a dilaton.
the localization of gauge fields in a 4D brane-world scenario, in which the dilaton plays an important role, in the context of the Kalb-Ramon field.
a complete description of the massless and massive gauge-field spectra, as well as with the localization conditions of these fields in the brane-world scenario.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a brane-world model with dilaton and gauge fields is able to localize gauge particles into our world, without tachyons and with an infinite tower of massive KK states, in agreement with the hierarchy problem.
a 4D world is a consistent theory in which the dilaton coupling to gauge fields is not necessarily the same for all gauge fields.
our 4D world is not only populated by a massless tensor mode but also by a massive vector one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a brane-localized Kaluza-Klien mass spectrum is found in our model.
, by means of the dilaton, it is possible to control the localization of the gauge fields in a brane-world and the whole spectrum of gauge particles.
, in this scenario, the Kalb-Ramon field is the only one which could have a massless mode in 4D, whereas the electromagnetic field is massive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 4D world is a very good approximation of the 5D theory.
, in the presence of dilaton, the gauge spectrum is split in two branches.
, in a brane-world, the coupling between the gauge fields and the dilaton is crucial to understand the localization of massless and Kaluza-Klien states.
